claims.text: A QA tutor and a tutor each report that the Submit button stays grey after choosing B.

The earlier batch-14 review records two resolved cases in which browser zoom hid Submit below the visible area, rather than disabling it, and records rejection of a universal browser-zoom remedy.

citation.title: Reject a universal browser-zoom remedy for Submit reports

k:rp-submit-zoom-generalization-rejected.excerpt:
[PRIOR RECORD (advice_review; decision_status: tl_rejected; execution_status: not_executed; outcome_status: resolved_in_checked_tasks) - history, not a standing rule.]
## Evidence available at review

The September 7 support notes cover RP14-Z011 and RP14-Z012 on a training workstation. At 200% browser zoom, the bottom of the form, including Submit, lay below the visible area. The button was not observed to be disabled. Returning the browser to 100% exposed the button, and both tasks produced a submission receipt: SIM-SUB-RP14-Z011 and SIM-SUB-RP14-Z012.

No network error or server rejection was recorded. These two cases were already resolved before this advice review; no action in response to the rejected recommendation has been executed.

## Prior ThreadSense advice

Add a standard FAQ answer telling every tutor with a Submit problem to reset browser zoom to 100% before reporting the issue.

## Factual errors

### Q: What counts as a significant factual error?
An error that changes the central conclusion or the answer the user would act on. A nonessential background detail with no effect on the recommendation is minor.

### Q: The source link is dead. Should I penalize the factual claim?
Record that the citation could not be verified. A failed URL alone does not prove the claim is false. Distinguish access failure from an unsupported attribution or fabricated reference.

A tutor reports being able to score both answers but says clicking Submit does nothing on RP-1577. A QA tutor reports finishing the preference rubric but being unable to submit the pair on RP-3325. An engineer asks for the LT error state and time on RP-3412 and RP-5337, and says the wider cause is not confirmed in those threads. The earlier batch-15 handoff records three reports of a disabled Submit button after required fields were filled, an approved and recorded engineering handoff on September 28, and reproduction of a disabled control in one trace without a confirmed shared cause or repair. The earlier handoff remained open at 17:00 UTC on September 28, with no fix or successful submission recorded; it cautions that a similar button state does not establish the same cause. The earlier batch-14 review records two resolved cases in which browser zoom hid Submit below the visible area, rather than disabling it, and records rejection of a universal browser-zoom remedy. The team lead's October 1 batch announcement asks for examples to remain in its thread while scope is checked; that directive concerns example collection, not an engineering intake route.
